    Relative quantification of qPCR data (delta-delta Ct and Pfaffl)

    Source: R/bio-assays.R
    bio_qpcr_ddct.Rd

    Calculates relative expression from quantification cycle (Ct or Cq) values. Technical replicates are averaged within each sample and gene. Each target gene is normalised to the reference gene(s) and then to the mean of the control group. With the default amplification efficiency of 2 (100 percent) this is the 2^-ddCt method of Livak and Schmittgen (2001); gene-specific efficiencies give the Pfaffl (2001) ratio. Several reference genes are combined by the geometric mean of their relative quantities (Vandesompele et al., 2002).

    Usage

    bio_qpcr_ddct(
  .data,
  ct,
  gene,
  sample,
  group,
  reference_genes,
  control,
  efficiency = 2
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per well.

    ct, gene, sample, group

    <tidy-select> Columns holding the Ct value, gene name, biological sample and experimental group.

    reference_genes

    Character vector of reference (housekeeping) genes.

    control

    Level of group used as the calibrator.

    efficiency

    Amplification factor per cycle, between 1 and 2: a single number, or a named vector with one value per gene.

    Value

    A <bio_assay> with one row per sample and target gene: the sample, group and gene columns, ct_target, ct_reference, delta_ct, delta_delta_ct, fold_change and log2_fold_change. tidy() summarises the fold change per group with confidence intervals and Welch t-tests against the control.

    References

    Livak, K. J. and Schmittgen, T. D. (2001). Analysis of relative gene expression data using real-time quantitative PCR and the 2^-ddCt method. Methods, 25, 402-408. doi:10.1006/meth.2001.1262

    Pfaffl, M. W. (2001). A new mathematical model for relative quantification in real-time RT-PCR. Nucleic Acids Research, 29, e45. doi:10.1093/nar/29.9.e45

    Vandesompele, J. et al. (2002). Accurate normalization of real-time quantitative RT-PCR data by geometric averaging of multiple internal control genes. Genome Biology, 3, research0034. doi:10.1186/gb-2002-3-7-research0034

    Examples

    rq <- bio_qpcr_ddct(qpcr_sim, ct, gene, sample, treatment,
  reference_genes = c("gapA", "rpoD"), control = "control"
)
rq
